text:
mike: Heads up — CI perf suite flagged a regression on PR #8410. microbench batch latency jumped ~18%. artifacts: https://ci.internal/redwood/8410/artifacts :grimacing:

sara: Can you paste the perf diff (p50/p95) and the failing test name?

ci-bot: perf-suite v2 report attached for run 2140001220: tests/perf/test_batcher::test_end_to_end_latency -> threshold diff +18.7% (p50), +12.3% (p95). Full log: https://ci.internal/redwood/8410/perf-report.txt

mike: quick snippet: ```before: p50=12.3ms p95=34.1ms
after:  p50=14.6ms p95=38.3ms
delta:  +18.7% p50 (+2.3ms)```

aleks: I pulled the profile from the artifacts — kernel selector flipped for the typical batch shape. Previously we used `fast_attn_fused`; now it's choosing `generic_attn` for the same workload. profiler snippet: ```kernel: generic_attn  calls=1.2k avg=0.84ms
kernel: fast_attn_fused calls=0.0k avg=N/A```

jen: PR #8410 touched quantization heuristics and the batcher cost model, right? Did we change the kernel-selection thresholds in that patch?

mike: yes, the PR adjusted the selector's latency-cost threshold and the warmup policy for KV cache eviction. The change reduces cache retention during bursty traffic which seems to increase observed batch sizes during microbench warmup.

ryan: Can you repro locally? what's the exact command to run the failing bench?

mike: repro command I used: ```RUNTIME_KERNEL_SELECTOR=autoselect pytest tests/perf/test_batcher.py::test_end_to_end_latency -k batch -q --maxfail=1``` Reproduces on my A5000 stack with the PR branch checked out.

aleks: quick hypothesis: eviction-on-warmup -> more cache misses -> larger effective sequence windows for the selector -> it falls back to generic kernel which has worse throughput for these batch shapes. I can see increased KV miss rate in the artifact logs: ```kv_hits=0.62 -> 0.41 during warmup window```

jen: Are we blocked on the release until this is resolved? perf regression > our alert threshold.

mike: I think it's a rollback candidate. Options: (1) revert the heuristic commit in the PR, (2) add a temporary CI override forcing previous kernel selector behavior, or (3) tweak warmup eviction params and re-run. Revert is fastest.

ci-bot: perf-regressions: PR #8410 flagged. Marking as rollout-blocker.

sara: If we revert, let's add a test exercising the selector edge-case. I can draft a microbench asserting kernel choice for the common batch shapes.

ryan: I'll start a bisect across the branch range to pinpoint the exact commit that caused the flip if you want to try narrowing before revert.

mike: thanks — please reference the perf artifact above. If bisect finds the single commit, we can publish a minimal revert patch instead of the full PR revert. tagging @eng-runtime-oncall for visibility :eyes:

aleks: FYI I pushed a quick CI patch that sets `RUNTIME_KERNEL_OVERRIDE=fast_attn_fused` for the perf job to confirm throughput restores. If that fixes, we can gate on selector tests.

jen: good plan. If the override heals perf we can ship a hotfix and then re-evaluate selector heuristics with more profiling.

mike: cool. I'll open the revert PR as backup: https://git.internal/redwood/reverts/8410-revert. Keep me posted on bisect results. :thumbsup:
